newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH C.BANK SAYS MONETARY DEVELOPMENT POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: CZECH C.BANK SAYS MONETARY DEVELOPMENT POSITIVE.

text.p: The Czech National Bank said on Friday that it saw positive monetary development laying the groundwork for lowering inflation, but growth in wages and demand was still creating "partial imbalances".

"The lowering in the pace of growth of the money supply and keeping the exchange rate in the established fluctuation band creates favourable preconditions for lowering the inflation rate," the CNB said in a statement released on Friday after the bank's governing board meeting on Thursday.
The key measure of Czech money supply, M2, showed growth slowing to 17.6 percent at the end of July from 20.8 percent at the end of June.
When the effects of the $1.32 billion equity expansion at SPT Telecom a.s. were factored out, the M2 growth slowed to 17.1 percent end-July from 18.7 percent end-June.
But the CNB said on Friday that there were "still some partial imbalances" in the economy.

"A marked preponderance of domestic demand over supply continues, supported mostly by a continuation in wage growth, which is not proportional with the growth of productivity of work in the economy," the CNB said.
"Domestic demand is, to a large extent, covered by imports which contributes to the growing deficit in the trade balance."

In late June the CNB raised its discount rate to 10.5 percent from 9.5 percent and increased minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent in an effort to tighten the money supply and stifle domestic demand.
The central bank and government target was to lower annual inflation to eight percent by the end of 1996 but it has remained stubbornly above nine percent.
The bank added that it also saw an "improvement in the quality of the loan portfolios of banks" as the share of classified credit on the overall volume of loans had dropped by one percentage point.
The CNB did not say in its statement what the actual share of classified credit was, and a relevant official was not avaible for comment.
